bullets.title: Little, Big
bullets.creator: John Crowley
bullets.note: _Little, Big_ is simply one of the best novels I’ve ever read, and even that doesn’t do it justice. It is, as one reviewer put it, “mysteriously affecting.” Read a few of [the Amazon reviews here](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/k0udre388b6h4gmpoug/6qheh8h2r4xrr3/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYW1hem9uLmNvbS9MaXR0bGUtQmlnLUpvaG4tQ3Jvd2xleS1lYm9vay9kcC9CMDA1REI3TzBVL3JlZj10bW1fa2luX3N3YXRjaF8wP19lbmNvZGluZz1VVEY4JnFpZD0mc3I9I2N1c3RvbWVyUmV2aWV3cw==) to get a glimpse of what I mean. On top of that, I feel like it put me in an altered state of consciousness that often lasted for 6–12 hours, best described as a deep feeling of serenity. And yet, I’ve hesitated for weeks to put it into “5-Bullet Friday”! Why? Because I think it’ll only grab 10–20% of you. In fact, my brother gave me the paperback version in 2018, and I tried reading it three or four times over the past two years. I put it down after fewer than 50 pages in each attempt. So how’d I end up finishing it this time? **This go-round, I committed to reading at least 100 pages, reading daily, and reading the Kindle version.** Why? It’s partly because the prose is stunningly beautiful, but it’s unusual and requires close attention. It’s partly because there are a lot of characters introduced in the first 100 pages, and you need to keep them straight, which is why I also [posted a pic of a family tree](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/k0udre388b6h4gmpoug/kkhmh6h9wpzwwp/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaW5zdGFncmFtLmNvbS9wL0NBdFFPOEluUlZYLw==) (the last of the three photos in the post) to help everyone out. Last, author John Crowley uses exquisite and poetic vocabulary, but I needed the Kindle built-in dictionary quite a lot ([_borborygmus_](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/k0udre388b6h4gmpoug/58hvh7h9xw3xxe/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubWVycmlhbS13ZWJzdGVyLmNvbS9kaWN0aW9uYXJ5L2JvcmJvcnlnbXVz), anyone?). It all sounds like a lot of work, and—guess what?—it _is_ a lot of work. But hot damn, the payoff is just so, so delicious that it’s hard to describe. If you try it, don’t say I didn’t warn you. 8 out of 10 of you will think I’ve lost my mind. But 2 out of 10 will find this tale of hyperreality, unreality, concrete jungles, fairy tales, and dreams to be nearly magical in its effects. This book is special.

bullets.title: Francisco Goya
bullets.note: (March 30, 1746–April 16, 1828) was a Spanish romantic painter and printmaker. He is considered the most important Spanish artist of the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries and throughout his long career was a commentator and chronicler of his era. Immensely successful in his lifetime, Goya is often referred to as both the last of the Old Masters and the first of the moderns. He was also one of the great contemporary portraitists.

bullets.section: What I’ve been focused on and just committed $1 million to —
bullets.title: The MAPS Capstone Challenge
bullets.note:
Along with others, I’ve helped organize a $10 million challenge pledge for MAPS, the Multidisciplinary Association of Psychedelic Studies. I’m contributing $1 million.  
  
**Why would I put so much time, energy, and capital into this?  
  
Tens of millions of people worldwide suffer from post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Millions more have suffered from emotional and physical abuse but never get diagnosed. I would put myself in the latter category. On top of that, PTSD is notoriously difficult to treat and cure. Conventional treatments fail all the time.  
  
Never before has the treatment of trauma been more relevant.  
  
In good news, it appears that one odd candidate—MDMA-assisted psychotherapy—can produce results that practically defy belief. As one actual patient put it in the [_Trip of Compassion_](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/k0udre388b6h4gmpoug/48hvheh2l3wl82/aHR0cHM6Ly92aW1lby5jb20vb25kZW1hbmQvdHJpcG9mY29tcGFzc2lvbg==) documentary, “I felt like I went through 15 years of psychological therapy in one night.”Now, let’s look at data instead of anecdote: In MAPS’ completed Phase 2 trials with 107 participants, 56% no longer qualified for PTSD after treatment with MDMA-assisted psychotherapy, measured two months following treatment. **At the 12-month follow-up, 68% no longer had PTSD. Most subjects received just** **2–3 sessions** **of MDMA-assisted psychotherapy.** **All participants had chronic, treatment-resistant PTSD and** **had suffered from PTSD for an average of 17.8 years****.** On August 16, 2017, the FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation to MDMA for the treatment of PTSD.  
  
There is a clear path ahead to make MDMA a legal medicine for millions of people suffering from PTSD.  
  
And just as important: If we succeed on this path, MDMA will also set precedent and open the door for dozens of other therapeutic compounds, including psilocybin. This is why I’m putting my muscle behind this lead domino. It matters for much more than MDMA.  
  
The [MAPS Capstone Challenge](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/k0udre388b6h4gmpoug/n2hohvhoq42q0k/aHR0cHM6Ly9jYXBzdG9uZS5tYXBzLm9yZy8=) will help provide the funds—$30 million total—needed to complete the studies required for FDA approval of MDMA-assisted psychotherapy for PTSD.MAPS has already raised $10 million. **If another $10 million are raised by September 10th, this will unlock a $10 million challenge pledge that I’ve helped put together, alongside PSFC, getting us to the finish line**. Half of the pledge comes from the [Steven & Alexandra Cohen Foundation](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/k0udre388b6h4gmpoug/reh8hoh5dpkdz0/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuc3RldmVhbmRhbGV4Lm9yZy8=) ([@cohengive](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/k0udre388b6h4gmpoug/08hwh9h7e4ner2/aHR0cHM6Ly90d2l0dGVyLmNvbS9jb2hlbmdpdmU=)), and the rest is split equally between me; James Bailey from Bail Capital; Peter Rahal, the founder of RXBAR ([@peterrahal](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/k0udre388b6h4gmpoug/8ghqhoh5d8wdnq/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaW5zdGFncmFtLmNvbS9wZXRlcnJhaGFsLw==)); Blake Mycoskie, the founder of TOMS ([@blakemycoskie](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/k0udre388b6h4gmpoug/vqh3hrhk06m0rg/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaW5zdGFncmFtLmNvbS9ibGFrZW15Y29za2llLz9obD1lbg==)); and one anonymous donor I hope to say more about soon.  
  
This challenge pledge is all or nothing. If MAPS fails to raise $10 million by September 10th, they do not receive the $10 million challenge pledge. There is no partial credit, and there is a real urgency. **This $10M challenge pledge was announced today in** [**my interview with Rick Doblin**](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/k0udre388b6h4gmpoug/l2hehmhk2pq27w/aHR0cHM6Ly90aW0uYmxvZy8yMDIwLzA2LzExL3JpY2stZG9ibGluLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWNvbnZlcnRraXQmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1jb252ZXJ0a2l0JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj01YmY=)**, the founder of** [**MAPS**](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/k0udre388b6h4gmpoug/m2h7h5hn5x25z2/aHR0cHM6Ly9tYXBzLm9yZy8=)**.** Please give it a listen, as we cover many other topics and stories.  
  
Every dollar matters, so if the spirit moves you, please consider giving what you can [by clicking here](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/k0udre388b6h4gmpoug/n2hohvhoq42q0k/aHR0cHM6Ly9jYXBzdG9uZS5tYXBzLm9yZy8=). **If you can contribute $100,000 or more over two years, please get in touch with Rick and his team by emailing** [**capstone@maps.org**](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/k0udre388b6h4gmpoug/e0hph7hnvzmvov/bWFpbHRvOmNhcHN0b25lQG1hcHMub3Jn)**.
